subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public contract be nested/per-agent `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` rather than the requested top-level `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The source shows the implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes the SSRF boundary and current maintainer discussion has not approved the final API shape or metadata/link-local/redirect/cache policy.

options.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
options.body: Land a default-off nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit output, docs, cache separation, and metadata/redirect tests.

options.title: Add Global Top-Level Opt-In
options.body: Expose the simpler global `allowPrivateNetwork` key and accept the larger compatibility and security-policy surface as a deliberate public contract.

options.title: Reject Broad Private Access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct operators to trusted proxies, fake-IP-specific flags, or separate internal-service tooling.

recommendation.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
recommendation.body: Land a default-off nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit output, docs, cache separation, and metadata/redirect tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of recent SSRF/web_fetch history and maintainer-context review on the rejected top-level shape.
